response: Yes, increased neutrophil migratory activity after major trauma is a factor in the etiology of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Research has shown that major blunt trauma enhances the migratory capacity of circulating neutrophils, which is manifest within 2 hours of admission. This is likely due to alterations in interleukin-8 receptor expression, affinity, or downstream signaling. In patients who later develop ARDS, initially elevated circulating neutrophil counts decrease rapidly over the same time course. The early enhanced neutrophil migratory activity, combined with elevated pulmonary concentrations of interleukin-8, may contribute to the establishment of the neutrophil infiltration that is characteristic of ARDS. Therefore, increased neutrophil migratory activity after major trauma plays a significant role in the development of ARDS.
